name: goal3_pooling
description: Goal 3: is pooling socks better or worse than each roommate keeping a separate drawer? Each pooled cell is matched to a solo cell of the same per-person capacity, so the comparison isolates pooling rather than drawer size: 64 socks shared by 4 is 16 each, against one roommate with 16 of their own. Note that C > unit*n + 10 forces a solo drawer to hold at least 16, which is why the pooled sizes are 64 and 80 rather than the default 40. The n=1 cells stand in for the four separate drawers: each is swept over the same seeds, so the aggregate across seeds is the distribution a single roommate faces alone.
